NO ISSUES

I found no violation I can back with a quoted rule and a quoted added line.

Findings I considered and dismissed, for the human review log:

1. **No ADR for the "defaults overwrite the user's `~/.claude/settings.json` at every start" decision.**
   - Rule: "Record decisions and glossary terms with the domain-modeling skill."
   - The PR does add the glossary term "Claude default settings". The overwrite behavior is stated in `docs/usage/coder-template.md` and the PR body, and the PR calls the door two-way ("merging under the user's own values can come later").
   - The rule does not say when a decision needs an ADR, so I could not make a quotable violation. A human may still want an ADR next to 0012 and 0016.

2. **`claude-default-settings.json` repeats most of the repo's own `.claude/settings.json`.**
   - Rule: "YAGNI, KISS, DRY."
   - The two files serve different audiences: this repo's own Claude sessions versus workspace users. I could not show the duplication is wrong, so I did not raise it.

3. **Comments in the new service file.**
   - Rule: "A comment says why: a constraint, gotcha or rejected alternative the code cannot show."
   - The comments on `Before=` ordering and on `cp` instead of `install` give constraints and a rejected alternative, so they comply.

4. **README currency.**
   - Rule: "Keep it current as the repo evolves, and brief".
   - No README line is shown to be stale by this diff.

NO ISSUES

I ran the durable-knowledge audit in diff mode over the added lines and found nothing that breaks a rule. I did not confirm anything against the unchanged working tree, so each KEEP below rests on the diff alone. Every finding was dropped at the high-signal bar.

| Anchor | Added text | Pattern | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLOSSARY.md, "Claude default settings" | "The Claude Code user settings the Coder template image gives every workspace user, taking precedence over the user's own." | Definition | KEEP | It states the domain meaning and one constraint, with no implementation detail. The `_Avoid_:` line follows the existing glossary format. |
| docs/usage/coder-template.md, new bullet | "written over `~/.claude/settings.json` at every workspace start, so a change made there lasts only until the next start; `~/.claude.json` and project settings are untouched." | Constraint | KEEP | It states a user-facing consequence and a scope boundary. It has no provenance and no rejected alternative. |
| claude-default-settings.service, line 119 comment | "# Claude pre-approval adds to the same file, and remote control must start with the defaults in place." | Comment | KEEP | It explains the `Before=` ordering, which the unit line alone does not show. |
| claude-default-settings.service, line 126 comment | "# cp, not install: it writes through a symlinked file (a dotfiles checkout's, say) instead of replacing the link." | Rejected alternative | KEEP | The rejected alternative is absent from the code, and the comment gives the constraint that excludes it. The smoke test enforces that constraint with its symlink checks. |
| smoke.sh, shellcheck comment | "# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq's own $d" | Comment | KEEP | It says why the lint is disabled, which the code cannot show. |

The README, ADR and domain.md rules raise nothing here: the diff touches none of them, and the changed docs add no code, diffs or file listings beyond a single file path.

One issue, and it blocks.

### 1. `cp` will not write through a dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink, so the Claude default settings are never applied

- **Path:** `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service`
- **Line (RIGHT side):** 12, `ExecStart=/bin/cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json %h/.claude/settings.json`
- **Reason:** bug
- **Blocks:** yes (a wrong outcome)

**Description:** The unit's comment, the PR body and the glossary entry all say the defaults are written through a dotfiles symlink. GNU `cp` does that only when the link's target already exists. When the target is missing, GNU `cp` refuses with `cp: not writing through dangling symlink`, unless `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set, and the oneshot fails.

The script that handles the same file next, `claude-pre-approval`'s `merge()`, deliberately resolves the link with `readlink -f` and creates the missing target as `{}`. So the two writers of this file disagree on exactly the symlink case this PR is meant to handle.

`agent-services.target` only `Wants=` the new unit, and the template's `systemctl --user start agent-services.target` succeeds whether or not that unit fails. So the failure is silent: pre-approval and remote control start anyway.

**Trigger:** the persistent `/home/dev` volume holds `~/.claude/settings.json` as a symlink into a dotfiles checkout whose target file does not exist. For example, a link created before the file, or the target deleted or renamed in the dotfiles repo. This is the same layout the smoke test sets up, minus the target file.

**Path:** `templates/coder/main.tf@coder_agent.main.startup_script` (`systemctl --user start agent-services.target`) → `images/coder-template/agent-services.target@Wants` → `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` (`/bin/cp … %h/.claude/settings.json` onto the dangling link) → the unit fails → `images/coder-template/claude-pre-approval.service` still runs, because it is only ordered `After` the unit, not `Requires=` it → `images/coder-template/claude-pre-approval@merge`.

**Outcome:**
- **Trust choice off:** the link stays dangling. `claude-default-settings.service` fails at every workspace start, and remote control and every Claude session run with none of the defaults: no `permissions.deny`, no `defaultMode: auto`, no `autoMemoryEnabled: false`, and so on.
- **Trust choice on:** `merge` creates the target as `{"enableAllProjectMcpServers": true}` only. Remote control then starts without the defaults for that whole start. The defaults appear only at the next workspace start.
- **Either way:** the unit is in a failed state, and nothing in the workspace start surfaces it.

**Suggested fix:** write to the resolved path, the same way `merge()` does. For example:

```
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'exec cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$(readlink -f "$HOME/.claude/settings.json")"'
```

Alternatively, run a small script that shares `merge`'s symlink handling.

**Test coverage (same finding, does not block on its own):** `images/coder-template/smoke.sh` covers only a fresh home (lines 217–218) and a symlink whose target exists (lines 66–68, checked at lines 92–97). Add a case with a dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` link: assert that its target ends up holding the defaults and that the path is still a link.

### Checked and found sound
- **Start order:** the new unit's `Before=` on `claude-pre-approval.service` and `claude-remote-control.service`, together with the target's automatic `After=` on what it wants, makes the copy run before pre-approval's merge. Smoke lines 89–94 would catch the reverse order.
- **Re-run at each start:** `PartOf=` plus `RemainAfterExit=yes` makes the copy run again whenever the target is stopped and started.
- **File modes:** `cp` keeps the mode of an existing destination. A new file gets 0644 minus the umask, which is fine because the file holds no secret.
- **Turning trust off later:** the two pre-approval choices are `mutable = false` in the template, so the copy cannot wipe an approval through a choice changed after creation.
- **Smoke assertions:** they come after the target's start job completes, so they test what they claim.
- **JSON settings keys:** I could not confirm offline that keys such as `worktree.baseRef: "fresh"` and the `disable*` flags are valid, so I flagged none of them. Every key except `attribution.commit` and `enabledPlugins` is identical to the repo's own `.claude/settings.json`.

**Dismissed findings:** none.

CONFIRM — every part holds as written.

- **Trigger:** Nothing at the head commit prevents `~/.claude/settings.json` on the persistent home volume from being a symlink to a missing dotfiles target. `smoke.sh` tests only a link whose target exists, so this case is not covered.
- **Path:** `agent-services.target` has `Wants=` on both services, and `claude-default-settings.service` has only `Before=` ordering on `claude-pre-approval.service`, no `Requires=`. When `cp` fails, `claude-pre-approval` and remote control therefore still start.
- **Outcome:** GNU `cp` refuses to write through a dangling destination symlink ("not writing through dangling symlink") unless `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set, so the oneshot fails. The unit's `Description` says it writes "over the user's at each start", but no other unit applies the defaults when `cp` fails. In `claude-pre-approval`, `merge` runs `readlink -f` on the link, which resolves the missing target path. It then writes `{}` there because `[ -s ]` fails, so the file ends up holding only `enableAllProjectMcpServers` when trust is on.

I did not trace `templates/coder/main.tf`, so the target being started by the agent startup script rests on the comment in `agent-services.target` and the candidate's path.

review.body: Title and description match the change. One blocking finding, inline: the new unit's `cp` does not write through a dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink, so in that case the Claude default settings are silently never applied. Everything else (unit ordering, re-run at each start via `PartOf=`/`RemainAfterExit=`, the smoke assertions, the glossary entry and the usage-doc note) looks sound.

comments.body:
**Bug (blocking): `cp` refuses to write through a dangling symlink, so the defaults are silently skipped.**

GNU `cp` writes through a symlinked destination only when the link's target already exists. When the target is missing it fails with `cp: not writing through dangling symlink`, unless `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set.

**Trigger:** the persistent home holds `~/.claude/settings.json` as a link into a dotfiles checkout whose target file does not exist. For example, the file was never committed, or it was renamed in the dotfiles repo.

**Path:** `agent-services.target@Wants` → this unit's `ExecStart` fails → `claude-pre-approval.service` and `claude-remote-control.service` still start. They are only ordered after this unit and do not `Requires=` it. → `claude-pre-approval@merge`.

**Outcome:**
- **Trust off:** the link stays dangling, this unit fails at every start, and Claude runs with none of the defaults (no `permissions.deny`, no `defaultMode`, no `autoMemoryEnabled: false`).
- **Trust on:** `merge` resolves the link with `readlink -f` and creates the target holding only `enableAllProjectMcpServers`. Remote control then starts without the defaults for that start.
- **Either way:** nothing surfaces the failed unit.

`merge()` in `claude-pre-approval` already handles this case by resolving the link first. Suggested fix: write to the resolved path the same way, for example:

```
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'exec cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$(readlink -f "$HOME/.claude/settings.json")"'
```

Then add a smoke case with a dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` link. It should assert that the link's target ends up holding the defaults and that the path is still a link.

candidates.claim: ExecStart's GNU cp refuses to write through a dangling ~/.claude/settings.json symlink (dotfiles target missing); the oneshot fails silently because agent-services.target only Wants it and pre-approval/remote control are only ordered after it, so the Claude default settings are never applied (trust off) or remote control starts with only enableAllProjectMcpServers (trust on). Smoke test lacks a dangling-link case.
candidates.validation: CONFIRM — every part holds as written. Trigger: nothing at the head commit prevents a dangling ~/.claude/settings.json symlink to a missing dotfiles target; smoke.sh only tests a link whose target exists. Path: agent-services.target Wants both services; claude-default-settings.service has only Before= ordering on claude-pre-approval.service, no Requires=, so when cp fails the rest still start. Outcome: GNU cp refuses to write through a dangling destination symlink unless POSIXLY_CORRECT is set, so the oneshot fails; merge in claude-pre-approval resolves the missing target with readlink -f and writes {} then enableAllProjectMcpServers when trust is on. (Did not trace templates/coder/main.tf; relied on agent-services.target's comment for the start path.)
